summary: Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies International Airport (YXC) serves the city of Cranbrook in southeastern British Columbia, acting as the main air gateway to the Canadian Rockies and the East Kootenay region. The airport provides year-round access to popular outdoor destinations including Kimberley, Fernie, and Kootenay National Park. Its elevated location and mountain surroundings give it a distinctive setting for travelers heading to alpine resorts and wilderness areas.
faqs:
Q: What airlines fly into Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies International Airport?
A: The airport is primarily served by Air Canada Express and WestJet Encore, offering scheduled flights to and from Calgary and Vancouver.

Q: How far is the airport from downtown Cranbrook?
A: The airport is located approximately 10-15 minutes north of downtown Cranbrook, making it a quick drive from the city center.

Q: Does the airport have customs and immigration services?
A: Yes, the airport operates as a port of entry with Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) facilities available for international flights.

Q: When is the best time to fly into YXC for skiing?
A: Winter months (December through March) are ideal for accessing nearby ski resorts like Kimberley Alpine Resort and Fernie Alpine Resort, though flights operate year-round.
transport_tips: Car rentals are available on-site and are the most convenient way to reach nearby destinations such as Kimberley or Fernie, as public transit options are limited. Taxi services and pre-arranged shuttles operate from the terminal, though booking in advance during peak ski season is recommended. The airport is conveniently located just off Highway 95A, providing easy road access to the broader Kootenay region.
local_tip: Pack layers in your carry-on—even in summer, temperatures at higher-elevation destinations like Fernie can be 10-15°C cooler than at the airport, and weather can shift quickly in the Rockies.
